source.title: Geometric Configurations of Perturbed Jailbreak Prompts
source.authors: Lynn Delcon; A. Algaba; Vincent Ginis

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: It uses SVM behavioral classification in last-layer, last-token embeddings to assess whether refusal/compliance has a linear direction, rather than the original difference-in-means measurement and causal ablation/addition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SVM results for separating compliance and refusal, which bear on V1's representational direction premise. Its GEE results report associations between first next-token strings and unsafe answers, but do not test whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction. SVM results for separating control and jailbreak prompts and control paraphrases are not rows because they concern prompt form, not refusal behavior.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its only result touching refusal is a linear SVM separating compliance from refusal (labelled by Llama Guard 4) among jailbreak prompts, using last-layer, last-token embeddings. V1 concerns a different thing: a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, usually taken from intermediate layers and post-instruction positions, that causally mediates refusal when ablated or added. The study builds no such direction, contrasts no harmful and harmless prompts, and runs no intervention. Its Discussion says the results do not support Arditi et al.'s direction, but the measure cannot show V1's effect. Its numbers are also ambiguous: balanced accuracy is 0.677 to 0.960, well above chance. The finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that embedding separability reflects spelling and template, not behavioural robustness. They find the top-50 probability space effectively one-dimensional and not organised by safety. In their refusal-dominated answer set, neither space shows (un)safe behaviour, and they see no clear refusal direction in the chosen embedding space. The paraphrase should add that they state this despite SVM balanced accuracies of 0.68 to 0.96, and that they flag the scarcity of compliant answers as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SVM classification of compliance/refusal and GEE associations with next-token probabilities; it does not use the original difference-in-means direction or ablate/add that direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The study notes that results may be obscured by the small number of compliant answers for some models and that GEE associations should be interpreted cautiously because prompt features repeat across prompts and independence assumptions are not fully met.

fits_no_version.finding: A linear SVM on last-layer, last-token embeddings separates compliance from refusal among jailbreak prompts with balanced accuracy 0.677 to 0.960 across six instruct models. The authors describe no clear visual separation and say the results do not support a refusal direction in this space.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In final-layer, last-token embeddings of perturbed jailbreak prompts, the answer label (safe or unsafe) is only moderately linearly decodable, and prompt form dominates the geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: The GEE regression links first next-tokens to the Llama Guard label. 'Sure' goes with unsafe answers in Qwen-1.5B. The Llama-1B tokens have sign-ambiguous directions. No token is linked to unsafe answers in the larger models, though Llama-8B has tokens significantly linked to safe answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How the first next-token relates to jailbreak success varies by model and is mostly weak.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted for the 2nd Workshop on Safe AI at UAI (SafeAI 2026)
record.problems: The paper reports few compliant answers for some tested models, which the authors say could hide effects. The prompt set is specific to Pliny-style jailbreaks, and the authors caution that repeated jailbreak features weaken the GEE independence assumption. SVM behavioral classification is not a causal intervention and does not establish that a refusal direction mediates behavior. The abstract's direction for two Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct token associations conflicts with the coefficient-sign convention stated for Table 7.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted SVM results separating control and jailbreak prompts or their paraphrases because they measure prompt form rather than refusal behavior. Did not include the GEE paraphrase-family coefficients because the paper's reported family-level trend is not a test of any listed direction or mechanism version; the token association outcomes most directly reported as behavior findings are retained.

untested.parts: All of it: no difference-in-means direction, no ablation or addition, no layer or position sweep, no capability check.
Jailbreak prompts are used, but nothing tests whether they suppress a refusal direction, and there is no adversarial training.
The authors state their design cannot separate harmfulness from atypical templates.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the reader's 'tests/T2' with a 'challenges' label on V1 to 'discusses'. The probe differs from V1 in layer (last only), contrast (compliant vs refusal within harmful jailbreaks, not harmful vs harmless), and method (classification, no causal intervention). Its above-chance accuracies do not show absence. Workshop paper; the GEE independence assumption is acknowledged as violated.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not construct the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, ablate or add it, test effects across all layers and positions, or evaluate retained general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The paper does not test whether attacks suppress a refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
It does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
The authors state their prompt design cannot distinguish harmfulness from atypical templates, but do not test separate harmfulness and refusal representations.
It studies multiple model families, but does not test transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
It does not vary refusal-training methods or stages to test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Behavioral-direction analysis in last-layer-last-token embeddings across the six tested instruct models
reader_labels.reason: The authors say their results do not support a clear refusal direction in this embedding space; the SVM scores assess linear classification only and do not establish causal mediation (svm_qwen15, svm_qwen3, svm_qwen7, svm_llama1, svm_llama3, svm_llama8).
